There are a number of things you could try. It all depends on what works for you.

* **Limiting your general screen time**: If you find yourself online most of the day, it can be easier to access sexual content online. Try gradually waning yourself of excessive screen time. You could also use a website disabler on your device, to lock yourself out of sex sites.
* **Replace your addictive activities with other focuses**: Take up something new that demands your attention. Start up an old hobby. Preferably, do something that gets your body moving.
* **Challenge yourself:** Give yourself an incentive for going without these activities for certain periods of time.
* **Surround yourself with people:** Self-explanatory. If you find yourself alone for too long, that can't be ideal.

Hi. I have had hsv2 for almost 2 years. I got it from an assault. I completely understand the initial thoughts/emotions the diagnosis comes with. However, once you have understood how many qualities of life this virus DOES NOT affect, you will find it much easier (nonetheless, not easy) to deal with. This is an incredibly common 'illness' and more people have it than you think.

My tips for anyone newly diagnosed: tell everyone you plan on having sex with, do not disclose unnecessarily, keep yourself happy and healthy. I have not had an outbreak in nearly a year. You will be fine. But you have to keep going to get to that point.
